description: Simulate the chapter's deterministic SGR policy for unit-value packets in a bounded multi-queue switch.

source.title: Packet Switching in Multi-queue Switches
source.algorithm_attribution: SGR (Semi-Greedy), unit-value case, with smallest-index queue tie-breaking.

workspace.meaning: Bounded queue loads, historical peaks, and staged slot trace.

contract.arrival_and_capacity: At each slot, per-queue arrivals are admitted up to the queue capacity; excess unit-value packets are dropped. This is equivalent to retaining any subset under the chapter's unit-value overflow rule.
contract.historical_peak: After admission, record the maximum load observed for each queue during the current busy period, including the current slot.
contract.rule_1: If any queue load exceeds floor(queue_capacity/2), transmit from a queue of maximum current load.
contract.rule_2: Otherwise, if any nonempty queue has historical peak below queue_capacity, transmit from the maximum-load queue in that subset.
contract.rule_3: Otherwise transmit from a maximum-load queue overall.
contract.ties_and_idle: Break ties by smallest queue index. Record -1 when all queues are empty. Reset all historical peaks when the switch becomes empty.
contract.scope: Unit packet values only. General QoS values, randomized RS, and competitive-ratio analysis are not implemented.
contract.error_results: Malformed input returns -1. Null output or capacity below 8*slot_count returns -2 without writes.

oracle_method: The primary oracle simulates queue loads and SGR rules directly. The independent verifier derives an active candidate set and selects the lexicographically highest (load, -queue_index) priority.
